title: Special mercy certain promise is presumption, not faith necessary object (Bellarmine)
source_text: XXIII. Sed inter varia illa fidei justificantis objecta Doctores Scholae Romanae negant esse promissionem specialis misericordiae, quin potius certam promissionem specialis misericordiae, non tam ad fidem quam ad praesumptionem pertinere contendunt: ut testatur Bellarminus, lib. 1. de Justif. cap. 4. sub finem. Et cap. 8. probare conatur fidem esse justificantem, quamvis non respiciat misericordiam specialem; imo non esse justificantem, si eam misericordiam forte respiciat. Quin ipse Vasquez contendit, cum caeteris, misericordiam Dei specialem non esse objectum fidei necessarium, ut haereticos confingere dicit: cum tamen ad justificationem requirat particularem fidem & fiduciam divinae promissionis & misericordiae, ut uberius infra explicabitur. Sed quod negare intendit illud est ad fidem justificantem necessarium esse, ut quisque credat sibi peccata esse remissa. Quod & alii intelligunt, dum negant misericordiam specialem ad objectum fidei justificantis spectare.
pass_a_gloss: But among those various objects of justifying faith the Roman doctors deny that the promise of special mercy belongs; rather they contend that a certain promise of special mercy pertains not so much to faith as to presumption, as Bellarmine witnesses (De Justif. 1.4 near the end). And in chapter 8 he tries to prove that faith is justifying even though it does not regard special mercy; indeed that it is not justifying if it happens to regard that mercy. Vasquez himself with the rest contends that God special mercy is not a necessary object of faith, as he says heretics invent, though for justification he does require a particular faith and trust in the divine promise and mercy, as will be explained more fully below. What he means to deny is that it is necessary to justifying faith that each person believe his own sins are remitted. Others understand the same when they deny that special mercy belongs to the object of justifying faith.
pass_b_english: Roman doctors refuse to count a certain promise of special mercy among justifying faith objects; Bellarmine treats that as presumption rather than faith (De Justif. 1.4; 1.8).

Vasquez and others deny special mercy is a necessary faith-object, as they say heretics invent, while still requiring particular trust in divine promise for justification; what they reject is that each must believe his own sins already remitted as faith necessary object.

lemmas.gloss: that his sins are remitted to him

choices.why: Rome rejects remitted-sins certainty as faith-object.
rejected: certainty of own remitted sins as necessary faith-object
